name: Honeywell MS7503 direct-coupled spring-return economizer actuator (27 lb-in, 2-10 Vdc)
function: 24 VAC powered, 27 lb-in spring-return actuator taking a 0(2)-10 Vdc command from the JADE; 2 V = closed, 10 V = full open. 90 s drive time, spring returns closed in under 25 s on power loss, 2-10 Vdc feedback output (JADE's 2-10 V output has no feedback input, so ACT POS shows n/a).

designation.value: Economizer actuator on JADE terminals ACT 2-10 (signal), ACT COM, ACT 24V

location.value: Direct-coupled onto the economizer damper shaft
location.source: docs/manuals/honeywell-ms7103-ms7503-specdata.pdf (Honeywell 31-00141M-03, MS7103/MS7503 3 Nm spring return DCA) p.1
location.note: MS7503 is a direct coupled actuator; damper location depends on the economizer installed.

lennox-lch240.sequenceRole: Holds minimum position when occupied, modulates for free cooling and DCV, closes when unoccupied / on shutdown.

partNumber.note: MS7503A3008 used earlier is not a listed model.

failureModes.name: No response to signal
failureModes.goodVsBad: Good 24 VAC + valid 2-10 Vdc, shaft doesn't move, no motor noise. Dead electronics or motor.
failureModes.symptoms: Damper stuck at last position (or closed if spring return lost power).

failureModes.name: Stalled / stripped gear train
failureModes.goodVsBad: Hums or clicks, shaft barely moves or slips.
failureModes.symptoms: Damper creeps or won't reach position.

failureModes.name: Poor tracking
failureModes.goodVsBad: Shaft position off from the command by more than the tracking tolerance.

failureModes.name: Slow stroke
failureModes.goodVsBad: Full stroke takes much longer than rated.

test.meter: VAC for power, VDC for signal, protractor/scale on the shaft indicator for position, stopwatch for stroke time.
procedure: Measure 24 VAC at the actuator supply leads (24 VAC ±20%). No power = not the actuator.
Measure the 2-10 Vdc command at the actuator, not at the JADE, to prove the wire.
Compare shaft position to command: % ≈ (V - 2) / 8 x 100. Full stroke takes about 90 s.

Shaft not moving? Lock out, then loosen the shaft adapter and move the damper by hand to check for binding. Do not twist the actuator itself: Honeywell says never turn the motor shaft by hand or with a wrench.
Damper free and actuator still won't track a valid signal = actuator.
Use JADE CHECKOUT > DAMPER OPEN / DAMPER CLOSE to drive full stroke and time it.
safety: Keep hands out of blades and linkage when power or signal is applied.
Never turn the actuator motor shaft by hand or with a wrench. It can destroy the motor (31-00141M-03).
Spring return drives the damper closed in under 25 s when power drops. Expect it to move when you lock out.

powerVac.source: docs/manuals/honeywell-ms7103-ms7503-specdata.pdf (Honeywell 31-00141M-03, MS7103/MS7503 3 Nm spring return DCA) p.1
powerVac.note: 24 VAC ±20%, Class 2. The JADE ACT ERROR guidance for Sylk actuators uses 21.6-26.4 V (63-2700-11 p.24).

strokeSecondsMax.source: docs/manuals/honeywell-ms7103-ms7503-specdata.pdf (Honeywell 31-00141M-03, MS7103/MS7503 3 Nm spring return DCA) p.1
strokeSecondsMax.note: Rated drive time is 90 s (manual). Treating >150 s as worn is an app rule of thumb.

symptoms.customer: "Stuffy in here," "bills high," "humid," depending on where it's stuck.
symptoms.tech: JADE DAMPER OUT says one thing, blades show another.

confusedWith: Bound damper blades / seized jackshaft bearings
Slipped shaft coupling (actuator turns, blades don't)
Missing 2-10 signal (controller, wiring, or no OCC/fan input)
JADE ACTUATOR SLIPPAGE ALARM (PC MOD tool, enabled by default) can flag a slipped coupling from the air-temperature check

labCases.context: Bench check after removing it to replace a bent jackshaft.
labCases.explanation: 6 V commands 50%; shaft at 51%. Strokes in 95 s. Healthy.

labCases.context: Damper stuck shut. 10 Vdc at the actuator, 24 VAC present.
labCases.explanation: Full command, good power, zero movement, silent. Dead actuator.

labCases.context: Damper creeps but never opens fully.
labCases.explanation: Hums, moves 12% with no load on it. The gear train is stripped. It wasn't the damper.
Tracks fine, but a 210 s stroke is way over rating. Motor or gears are wearing. Replace soon.
